home.problemHeading: Your process document is not your process.
home.problemLead: The real one has rework loops, people chasing each other for answers, and long stretches where a case just waits. A request can sit in a queue for days and need only minutes of actual work. Automate the documented version and you automate the wrong thing.
home.problemKicker: The waiting is the process. The work is minutes.
home.discoveryHeading: How we find the real process
home.discoveryLead: We look at the work from three sides, because each one shows something the others miss.

discovery.title: Interviews: the why
discovery.body: We talk to the people who do the work: who decides, which workarounds they rely on, and the thresholds nobody wrote down.

discovery.title: Your systems' logs: the what
discovery.body: Your ERP, CRM and helpdesk record every case, so we can see how many arrive, how long each step takes, where cases wait and which ones loop back.

discovery.title: Everything else
discovery.body: Procedures, spreadsheets, email threads and chat hold the exceptions and rules your systems never captured.

home.bucketsLead: In that order. Most teams start with the model.

buckets.title: Delete
buckets.body: Steps that exist because of an old workaround, a duplicate check or a report nobody reads. A deleted step costs nothing to run.

buckets.title: Plain code
buckets.body: Steps with fixed rules: copy this field, send that reminder, match these two amounts. Ordinary software does them reliably and cheaply.

buckets.title: An agent
buckets.body: Steps that need reading and judgement within clear limits, such as an unstructured email, a mismatched invoice or a missing document. The agent prepares the case.

buckets.title: A person
buckets.body: Decisions with consequences: approvals, exceptions and negotiations. The agent hands them over with the context attached, and a person makes the call.

home.stepsLead: You give us access to the work and the people who do it. We do the mapping, the building and the measuring.

steps.title: Map the real process
steps.body: Interviews, system logs and documents show how the work really moves, including the loops and the waiting.

steps.title: Set the baseline
steps.body: Before we build anything, we measure volume, cycle time, waiting time and exceptions, so the result can be compared with today.

steps.title: Sort and build
steps.body: We delete what shouldn't exist, write plain code for the fixed rules and build agents for the steps that need judgement. Each process has one owner on your side.

steps.title: Measure and expand
steps.body: We measure the same numbers again. Once the process holds, we move on to the next one.

home.systemsHeading: Built on the systems you already run
home.systemsLead: You keep your ERP, your CRM and your helpdesk. Agents connect to them and work by your rules.

systems.title: Connected to your stack
systems.body: Agents work through the APIs of your ERP, CRM, helpdesk and data platforms, with only the permissions you grant.

systems.title: A person makes the call
systems.body: Agents prepare each case and stop at the decision. Approvals and exceptions go to the person who owns them.

systems.title: A record of every action
systems.body: Every decision and change is logged, so your team and your auditors can see what happened and why.

about.heading: Building AI since before ChatGPT.
body: I lead the agency. Before ChatGPT, I founded an AI company that built models of every kind to automate fraud and security work. A company in San Francisco acquired it, and I went on to work there.
There we built AI, and the processes around it, where it had the most impact. We adopted new advances while they were still at an early stage and reached very high levels of automation.
The agency brings that experience to your operations. We've worked on processes of every kind, and each engagement starts the same way: finding out how the work really runs.
about.photoAlt: Portrait of the person who leads the agency

home.faqHeading: Questions we hear on first calls

faqs.q: What happens on the discovery call?
faqs.a: We pick one process and map how it really runs: who touches it, where cases wait and where they loop back. You leave with a first view of which steps to delete, which to automate and which to keep with a person, whether or not we work together.

faqs.q: How long until the first agent is live?
faqs.a: It depends on the process and how many systems it touches. We agree a timeline once the process is mapped, and we set the baseline before we build anything.

faqs.q: What can the agents actually do?
faqs.a: They read documents and messages, update your systems, check each case against your rules and gather the evidence for a decision. Then they stop and hand the decision to a person, with the context attached.

faqs.q: Do the agents work with the tools we already have?
faqs.a: Yes. They connect through APIs to ERPs, CRMs, helpdesks, databases and data platforms, so you keep the systems your team knows.

faqs.q: How much of our team's time will it take?
faqs.a: Most of it comes at the start, in interviews about how the work really runs, followed by short reviews of the design. We do the building and the running.

faqs.q: How do you handle security and data?
faqs.a: Agents run inside your existing permissions and security policies, and every action is logged and auditable. We can work under your data processing agreement.

faqs.q: How do you know it worked?
faqs.a: We measure the process before we build: volume, cycle time, waiting time and exceptions. After launch we measure the same things again and show you the comparison.
It depends on the complexity of the workflow, the systems involved and the scope of the deployment. After the discovery call we send you a written proposal.

home.ctaHeading: Free up more than half of your team's time.
home.ctaLead: Agents take over the repetitive work: re-keying, chasing, matching. Your people keep the decisions. Bring one process to a call and we'll show you how much of it an agent can take.

useCases.headingLead: The same repetitive work shows up in every industry.
useCases.heading: This is where agents take it over.
useCases.lead: Every sector has its own systems, rules and paperwork, but the work that piles up looks alike: documents typed in by hand, people chasing each other for answers, cases waiting in a queue. Below are the processes we look at first in each industry and, for each one, how an agent handles it, sorted with our method.
useCases.markets: We serve companies in Spain, Italy, the United Kingdom and the United States, in English, Spanish and Italian.
useCases.legendLead: Each step below lands in one of four buckets, checked in this order:
useCases.exampleNote: Illustration of the method, not a client engagement.
useCases.ctaHeading: Bring one process from your own business.
useCases.ctaLead: Your industry isn't on this page? The method is the same. On the discovery call we map one of your processes and show you which steps to delete, which an agent can take and which stay with your team.

industries.name: Manufacturing
industries.lead: Production runs on the ERP, but customer orders, supplier confirmations and quality records still arrive as emails, PDFs and spreadsheets that someone has to type in.

cases.title: Customer order entry
cases.body: An agent reads purchase orders that arrive by email, checks prices and lead times against the ERP and creates the sales order. Orders that don't match go to a person with the difference marked.

how.step: Read the PDF order and extract items, quantities and dates
Check prices, stock and lead times in the ERP
Ask a colleague to re-check the order by eye
Accept a delivery date the plant can only meet with overtime

cases.title: Supplier confirmations and delays
cases.body: Agents read each order confirmation, compare dates and quantities with what was ordered, and flag the ones that put the production plan at risk.

how.step: Read each confirmation and compare it with the purchase order
Update the expected dates in the ERP
Keep a separate spreadsheet of late suppliers
Decide whether to move production or find another supplier

cases.title: Quality and non-conformance records
cases.body: An agent turns inspection notes and customer complaints into structured non-conformance reports, attaches the evidence and sends them to the quality lead.

how.step: Turn inspection notes and complaints into a structured report
Pull the batch and test records from your systems
Retype the report into the quality system by hand
Decide the root cause and the corrective action

cases.title: Supplier invoices
cases.body: Invoices arriving on paper, as PDFs or through e-invoicing networks such as Italy's SDI are matched to the order and the goods receipt. Only the exceptions reach accounts payable.

how.step: Read the invoice, whether it arrives on paper, as a PDF or through SDI
Match it to the order and the goods receipt
Print the invoice to collect approval signatures
Approve the invoices that don't match

industries.name: Distribution and logistics
industries.lead: Margins are thin and volumes are high, so every shipment exception, freight invoice and customer query handled by hand eats into the day.

cases.title: Shipment exceptions
cases.body: Agents follow carrier updates, spot the shipments that will arrive late, propose a way to recover them and warn customer service before the customer calls.

how.step: Pull the tracking status from each carrier
Read the carrier's message and work out the cause
Draft the message to the customer with the new date
Approve paying for express freight

cases.title: Freight invoice checks
cases.body: Plain code checks every carrier invoice against the agreed rates. When a charge differs, an agent works out why and prepares the dispute.

how.step: Check every charge against the agreed rates
Work out why a charge differs
Draft the dispute with the evidence attached
Decide which disputes are worth raising

cases.title: Delivery claims
cases.body: For a damaged or missing parcel, an agent collects the delivery note, the photos and the carrier's messages, and drafts the claim.

how.step: Collect the delivery note, the photos and the carrier's messages
Copy the same details into a claims spreadsheet
Draft the claim and submit it to the carrier
Accept or reject the carrier's offer

cases.title: Customs paperwork
cases.body: For cross-border shipments, such as between the UK and the EU, an agent prepares the commercial invoice and proposes the commodity codes. A person signs off.

how.step: Pull the order lines and weights from the ERP
Prepare the commercial invoice and propose the commodity codes
Email the draft round for comments
Sign off the declaration

industries.name: Retail and e-commerce
industries.lead: Orders, returns and supplier catalogues move fast, and the people behind them spend their days copying data between the shop, the marketplaces and the ERP.

cases.title: Returns and refunds
cases.body: An agent reads the return request, checks it against the policy and the order history and prepares the refund. Cases outside the policy go to a person.

how.step: Read the customer's message and photos
Check the return window and create the label
Ask the customer to fill in a second form with the same details
Approve a refund outside the policy

cases.title: Product data from suppliers
cases.body: Supplier catalogues arrive in every format. An agent maps them to your product fields, writes the missing descriptions in each language and flags gaps before a product goes live.

how.step: Map the supplier's catalogue to your product fields
Write the missing descriptions in each language
Check that every required field is filled in
Approve the product before it goes live

cases.title: Customer service triage
cases.body: Agents sort incoming messages, look up the order across your systems and answer the routine questions, such as where a parcel is. The rest reach your team with the order already looked up.

how.step: Sort each message by topic and urgency
Look up the order across your systems
Answer the routine questions, such as where a parcel is
Handle complaints and unusual requests

cases.title: Marketplace payouts
cases.body: Plain code matches each marketplace payout to its orders, fees and refunds. An agent investigates the payouts that don't add up.

how.step: Match each payout to its orders, fees and refunds
Rebuild the same match by hand in a spreadsheet
Investigate the payouts that don't add up
Decide which differences to claim from the marketplace

industries.name: Financial services and insurance
industries.lead: Regulated work runs on documents and checks: onboarding files, claims, policy changes. Much of the effort goes into collecting evidence and copying it from one system to the next.

cases.title: Client onboarding and KYC
cases.body: An agent collects the documents, checks that they are complete and consistent, runs the screening through your providers and prepares the file for the compliance officer.

how.step: Collect the documents and check that they are complete
Run the screening through your providers
Print the file to sign it on paper
Approve or reject the client

cases.title: Claims intake
cases.body: Agents read the first notice of a claim, pull the policy, ask for the missing documents and prepare the case for a handler, who decides.

how.step: Read the claim email and register the claim
Check that the policy was active on the date of the loss
Ask the customer for the missing documents
Decide whether to accept the claim, and for how much

cases.title: Policy and account changes
cases.body: Address changes, beneficiary updates and similar requests arrive by email. An agent completes the identity checks you require and updates the core system.

how.step: Read the request and work out what needs to change
Run the identity checks you require
Update the core system
Approve changes that affect a payout, such as a new beneficiary

cases.title: Evidence for regulatory reports
cases.body: An agent gathers the extracts and supporting evidence for each report, and a person reviews it before anything is filed.

how.step: Pull the extracts each report needs
Gather the supporting evidence and note any gaps
Send the draft round by email for everyone to check
Review and sign off before anything is filed

industries.name: Professional services
industries.lead: Accounting, law and consulting firms sell expert hours, yet many of those hours go into collecting documents from clients, filling in timesheets and preparing invoices.

cases.title: Collecting client documents
cases.body: An agent asks each client for what is missing, checks what arrives, files it in the right place and chases the rest. Your team works only on complete files.

how.step: Remind each client which documents are still missing
Check what arrives and file it in the right place
Keep a checklist for each client in a separate spreadsheet
Call the clients who still haven't sent anything

cases.title: Bookkeeping for clients
cases.body: In an accounting firm, agents classify bank movements and purchase invoices, propose the entries and leave the uncertain ones to the accountant.

how.step: Read invoices and receipts in any format
Classify each one and propose the entry
Reconcile the entries with the bank statement
Review the entries the agent wasn't sure about

cases.title: Conflict checks and engagement letters
cases.body: An agent searches past matters and contacts for conflicts and drafts the engagement letter from your templates. A partner approves both.

how.step: Search past matters and contacts for conflicts
Draft the engagement letter from your templates
Circulate the letter by email for comments
Approve the conflict check and the letter

cases.title: Time capture and billing
cases.body: An agent drafts time entries from calendars, email and documents, so people review their week instead of reconstructing it, and prepares the invoice for approval.

how.step: Draft time entries from calendars, email and documents
Rebuild the week from memory on Friday
Prepare the invoice from the approved entries
Review the week and approve the invoice

industries.name: Real estate and property management
industries.lead: Property managers juggle tenants, owners, contractors and invoices across many buildings, and most of their day is coordination.

cases.title: Maintenance requests
cases.body: An agent reads the tenant's message and photos, works out how urgent it is and which trade it needs, books a contractor from your approved list and keeps the tenant informed.

how.step: Read the tenant's message and photos
Work out how urgent it is and which trade it needs
Book a contractor from the approved list and update the tenant
Approve work above the spending limit

cases.title: Rent collection and arrears
cases.body: Plain code matches payments to leases. An agent follows up on missed payments in the tone your policy sets, and a person decides on payment plans.

how.step: Match payments to leases
Follow up on missed payments in the tone your policy sets
Send the same reminder by post and by email
Agree a payment plan with the tenant

cases.title: Contractor invoices
cases.body: Each invoice is matched to its work order and the agreed price, and charged to the right building and owner.

how.step: Read the invoice and find its work order
Check it against the agreed price
Charge it to the right building and owner
Approve the invoices above the agreed price

cases.title: Owner statements
cases.body: An agent prepares each owner's monthly statement and summary of works, so the team reviews them instead of building them.

how.step: Pull the rents, costs and works for each property
Write the month's summary of works
Email the owner separately about every small repair
Review the statement before it goes out

industries.name: Hospitality and travel
industries.lead: Hotels, tour operators and travel agencies handle bookings, changes and supplier invoices in seasonal peaks, and the back office has to keep up with the season.

cases.title: Group and event requests
cases.body: An agent reads the request, checks availability and rates and drafts the proposal for the sales team to send.

how.step: Read the request and pull out the dates, rooms and needs
Check availability and the rate rules
Draft the proposal from your templates
Set the price for a large group in high season

cases.title: Booking changes and cancellations
cases.body: Agents apply your conditions to each change, update the booking in the channel manager and the property system, and pass the exceptions to a person.

how.step: Read the request and apply your conditions
Update the channel manager and the property system
Copy the change into a shared spreadsheet
Decide on exceptions, such as a refund outside the conditions

cases.title: Supplier and commission reconciliation
cases.body: Plain code matches supplier invoices and booking-channel commissions to the bookings. An agent investigates the differences.

how.step: Match invoices and commissions to the bookings
Investigate the differences
Tick off each line by hand on a printout
Decide which differences to dispute

cases.title: Reviews and complaints
cases.body: An agent sorts reviews and complaints by topic and property, drafts the replies and sends recurring problems to the manager who can fix them.

how.step: Sort reviews and complaints by topic and property
Draft the replies
Send recurring problems to the manager who can fix them
Answer serious complaints personally

industries.name: Private healthcare
industries.lead: Clinics and practices lose staff time to insurer paperwork, referrals and billing. Agents work only on that administrative side, never on clinical decisions.

cases.title: Insurer authorisations
cases.body: An agent prepares the authorisation request with the documents the insurer asks for, submits it and follows it up. A person handles refusals.

how.step: Prepare the request with the documents the insurer asks for
Submit it and track the answer
Print the request for the patient's paper file
Handle refusals with the patient and the insurer

cases.title: Referrals and appointment requests
cases.body: Agents read referral letters and requests, check what each one needs and propose a slot, so reception confirms instead of typing.

how.step: Read the referral letter and work out what it needs
Propose a slot that fits the specialist and the tests
Retype the referral into the scheduling system
Confirm the appointment with the patient

cases.title: Billing to insurers
cases.body: Plain code builds the claims from the appointments. When an insurer rejects one, an agent works out why and prepares the correction.

how.step: Build the claims from the appointments
Read a rejection and work out the reason
Prepare the corrected claim
Decide whether to appeal or write it off

cases.title: Administrative messages from patients
cases.body: Agents answer routine questions about appointments, documents and invoices, and pass anything clinical straight to your team.

how.step: Sort the messages by topic and spot anything clinical
Look up appointments and invoices in your systems
Answer routine questions about appointments, documents and invoices
Answer anything clinical
